Definition: The share of units that come out right the first time, with no rework or scrap needed.
A standardized defect rate -- how many defects would occur per million chances for one, letting very different processes be compared on the same scale.
The total cost of things going wrong -- scrap, rework, returns, and warranty claims.
The share of material or units that had to be thrown away rather than used or sold.
Work that had to be redone because it didn't meet quality standards the first time.
The share of shipped units that were sent back as faulty or under warranty.
A quality methodology aimed at reducing process variation and defects to a very small, statistically defined rate.
Using statistics to monitor a process in real time and catch it drifting out of spec before it produces bad output.
The share of output that comes out good, out of everything started or processed.
The share of items produced that do not meet quality requirements.
The number of times customers formally report a problem with a product or service.
Products sent back by customers, shown as a count or as a share of sales.
The share of products or jobs that were done correctly the first time, with no rework or repair.
The chance that a unit passes through every step of a process without a defect, found by multiplying the first-pass yield of each step.
The average number of defects found on each unit inspected.
The number of defective items for every million produced or inspected.
The total number of defects found in a period.

Also known as: Percent Defective; Reject Rate; Rejection Rate
Definition: The share of inspected items that were found to be defective.

Also known as: Escaped Defects; Defects Found by Customers
Definition: The share of defects that were not caught in-house and were found by the customer instead.
The share of all defects that were found before the product reached the customer.
The total cost of making sure quality is right and of fixing it when it is wrong, including prevention, checking and failure costs.

Also known as: COPQ Percentage; Poor Quality Cost to Sales
Definition: The cost of poor quality shown as a percentage of sales.

Also known as: Internal Failure Costs; Cost of Internal Failure
Definition: The cost of problems found before the product leaves the business, such as scrap, rework and re-inspection.

Also known as: External Failure Costs; Cost of External Failure
Definition: The cost of problems found after the product has reached the customer, such as returns, warranty claims and recalls.
The money spent to stop quality problems happening in the first place, such as training, planning and design reviews.

Also known as: Appraisal Costs; Inspection Cost; Cost of Appraisal
Definition: The money spent on checking products and processes to find problems, such as inspection and testing.

Also known as: Cost of Scrap; Scrap Value; Scrap Loss
Definition: The value of material and effort lost on items that cannot be fixed or sold.
The number of units thrown away as unusable in a period.
The share of items that needed to be reworked before they could be accepted.
The cost of fixing items that were not right the first time, including labour and materials.

Also known as: Warranty Cost; Warranty Returns; Warranty Rate
Definition: The number or cost of claims made by customers under the product warranty.

Also known as: Warranty Cost to Sales; Warranty Expense Rate
Definition: The cost of warranty claims shown as a percentage of sales.

Also known as: Return Merchandise Authorisation Rate; RMA Rate; Customer Return Rate
Definition: The share of delivered items that customers sent back, usually because of a quality problem.
The number of customer complaints for every million units sold or delivered.
The share of customer complaints that were closed in a period.
A case where a product, process or service does not meet the requirement or specification.
A formal record raised when a non-conformance is found, which tracks the cause and what is done about it.

Also known as: NCR Closure Time; Time to Close NCR
Definition: The average time taken to close a non-conformance report from when it was raised.
The share of corrective actions that were closed by their due date.
Steps taken to remove the cause of a possible problem before it happens.
The share of problems for which the root cause was found and recorded within the target time.

Also known as: Recurring Defects; Repeat Issues; Repeat Non-Conformances
Definition: The number of problems that happened again after they had supposedly been fixed.

Also known as: Pass Rate; First Pass Inspection Rate; Acceptance Rate
Definition: The share of inspections that were passed.

Also known as: Receiving Inspection Reject Rate; Incoming Quality Rejection
Definition: The share of delivered goods that were rejected when checked on arrival.

Also known as: Outgoing Quality; Final Quality Pass Rate
Definition: The share of finished goods that passed the final check before being shipped.

Also known as: Audit Non-Conformities; Findings per Audit; Audit Observations
Definition: The number of problems or gaps noted during an audit.

Also known as: Audits Completed; Audit Plan Completion; Audit Schedule Adherence
Definition: The share of planned audits that were completed on time.
The overall score given after an audit, showing how well the area meets the requirements.

Also known as: Calibration On Time; Gauge Calibration Compliance; Calibrations Due
Definition: The share of measuring instruments that were calibrated by their due date.

Also known as: Document Compliance; Document Review Compliance; Overdue Documents
Definition: The share of controlled documents that are current and reviewed on time.

Also known as: Quality Training Completion; Training Completion Rate; Mandatory Training Rate
Definition: The share of required training that was completed by the people who needed it.

Also known as: Quality Index; Quality Rating; Overall Quality
Definition: A summary score of quality, usually combining several measures such as defects, returns and audit results.

Also known as: Vendor Quality Rating; Supplier Quality Index
Definition: A score showing the quality of goods received from a supplier.
A measure of how rarely a process makes a defect. A higher sigma level means fewer defects.

Also known as: Out of Control Points; SPC Alarms; Out-of-Control Points
Definition: The number of times a measured value moved outside the control limits, signalling that the process may have changed.

Also known as: Measurement System Analysis; MSA; Measurement Error
Definition: A test of how much of the variation in measurements comes from the measuring equipment and the people using it rather than the product.
A measure of whether a process can stay within its limits, compared with the width of the limits. A value above 1.33 is often seen as capable.

Also known as: Delivery Right First Time; Perfect Delivery
Definition: The share of deliveries made with the right product, quantity, quality and paperwork the first time.
The number of times products had to be taken back from customers because of a safety or quality problem.
The score given to the business by a customer who rates its quality, delivery and service.
The number of defective products that got past the checks and reached the next process or the customer.
The share of products accepted even though they did not fully meet the specification, with approval to do so.

Also known as: First Pass Rate; FPQ; First Time Through
Definition: The share of units that pass all checks the first time they go through a process.

Also known as: Defect Types; Defect Pareto; Defect Breakdown
Definition: A breakdown of defects by type, usually shown from the biggest to the smallest so the main causes stand out.

Also known as: Batch Acceptance Rate; Lot Pass Rate
Definition: The share of lots or batches that were accepted after inspection.
The amount lost during a process because the output was less than the input should have given.
